clue.text: Appreciating notes left after American's probed glass substitute?

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind what follows it, so it ends up last
to be probed is to have something pushed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: mica is a mineral once used in place of glass, as in stove windows
US for American
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone who has just stuck a finger into an artificial window pane is somehow enjoying music.
explanation.walkthrough: The word order is reversed: 'left after' puts L at the end, once the American has probed the glass substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical person is fond of and responsive to music, so is appreciating notes.

clue.text: Observing vessel entering China

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it

parts.note: Ming is a Chinese dynasty, and Ming china is its porcelain
Noah's ark, a ship

explanation.surface: Someone watches a ship sailing into Chinese waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes 'China' look like the country; it is porcelain, MING.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark is to notice or observe, as in mark my words, so marking is observing.

clue.text: Small and highly-regarded, though not right and not accurate

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter that stands for right

parts.note: S for small, as in clothing sizes
precious means greatly valued

explanation.surface: Something small and much admired may still turn out to be wrong and imprecise.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right drops out of PRECIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means plausible on the surface but actually wrong, so not accurate.

clue.text: That fellow's blocking Civil Service game

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for the Civil Service
he's, as in that fellow is

explanation.surface: A man is obstructing a government department's game.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game of kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: What may help you make slam or blast?

definitions.text: What may help you make slam
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in bridge, the final trump card held can win the trick needed for a slam
second meaning: the trumpet call that the Bible says will wake the dead on Judgement Day

explanation.walkthrough: A slam in bridge is winning all or all but one of the tricks, and trumps win tricks; 'blast' is a trumpet's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a card game's final trump and the biblical trumpet sounding at the end of the world.

clue.text: Stink filling middle of dustbins is something in hand

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so one piece goes within the other
asks for only the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: the two central letters of an eight-letter word
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A bad smell in the bins is something you can hold in your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum is informal British slang for a bad smell; 'filling' looks like food, but it means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb is a digit, one part of the hand, so literally something in a hand.

clue.text: Article poses timeless item for debate

indicators.note: without time, so the letter standing for time is removed

parts.note: the definite article
a model poses, or sits, for an artist; T for time goes

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece puts forward something lasting to be argued over.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward to be argued and defended, a matter for debate.

clue.text: University prepared to be stretched, having disposed of latest device

indicators.note: the latest is the last letter, and getting rid of it shortens the word

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
tensile means capable of being drawn out

explanation.surface: A university is ready to be pushed hard after scrapping its newest gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially in the kitchen, so a device.

clue.text: Vehicle with problems?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light carriage or a pushchair
second meaning: full of software faults

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a buggy is also a pushchair for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small carriage and, as an adjective, a program riddled with defects.

clue.text: Fielder sees large number of people reduced after interval

indicators.note: something reduced is cut short, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a third is a musical interval
the many, the masses

explanation.surface: A cricketer notices crowds thinning after the break in play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interval' suggests a break in a match, but here it is the musical gap between notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Third man is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the off side.

clue.text: Army soldiers ousting one from concealed position

indicators.note: ousting means pushing out and taking the place of, so the soldiers replace the letter for one

parts.note: a hide is a shelter from which to watch birds unseen
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Troops clear a hidden position of one occupant to take it over.
explanation.walkthrough: OR takes the place of the I in HIDE, giving HORDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd, and an army is likewise a huge number of people or things.

clue.text: Bridge player, say, engaged in some work, producing unexpected feature

parts.note: the four bridge players are named by compass points

indicators.note: something engaged in a task is occupied within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
e.g., for example, which is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A card player busy at some job turns up something surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The erg is a physics unit of work, and 'say' signals an example (e.g.).
explanation.definitionFit: An Easter egg is a hidden surprise put into software, a film or a game by its makers.

clue.text: Wet season securing island fruit

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: the rains are the monsoon season in the tropics
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A rainy season keeps a tropical island's fruit crop safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are dried grapes, a fruit sold dried for baking and snacks.

clue.text: Acquisitive King invading this territory's borders

indicators.note: an invader goes into a country, so this letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: taken as written
R for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A greedy king invades the edges of this land.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty can mean eager to get or have, as in thirsty for power, so greedy or acquisitive.

clue.text: Major work getting OUP excited, investing in lots of champagne

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and fall out of their order
to invest is to put something into another thing, as money into a venture

parts.note: a magnum is a double-size bottle, so magnums are a lot of champagne
the letters of the Oxford University Press abbreviation rearranged

explanation.surface: Oxford University Press celebrates a major publication by putting money into vast amounts of champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnum opus is Latin for great work, a writer or artist's most important achievement.

clue.text: A second drink for the wife?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: another half pint of beer
second meaning: a jokey term for one's spouse

explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub a half is a half-pint, so 'the other half' is a further drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Other half is informal for a spouse or partner, and also a further half-pint.

clue.text: Obscure publicity material ignoring second book

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a blurb is promotional text, as on a book jacket
B for book; the second one in the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A publisher's dull promotional copy that leaves out its second title.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two Bs; only the second, final one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur is to make indistinct, which is to obscure as a verb.

clue.text: Radio's studied later, after accident or crisis?

indicators.note: an accident leaves things jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
on the radio words are heard rather than seen, so we go by sound

parts.note: past tense of read, spoken alike to the colour
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's learning comes later, after an accident or emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Red alert is the highest state of readiness for danger, so a crisis, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Revision of poor plan's outputting new suggestion

indicators.note: a revision reworks the original, so these letters are put in a fresh order
putting out a letter means it goes from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written for the mix
N for new

explanation.surface: Rewriting a weak plan produces a fresh suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N for new from the letters of poor plans, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a plan or idea put forward for consideration, a suggestion.

clue.text: Reputation held by pair of Americans?

indicators.note: only what is held inside is kept, so the outer letters are thrown away

parts.note: two of them written side by side

explanation.surface: A good reputation is shared by two people from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Write AMERICAN twice; the end of the first runs into the start of the second, americaNAMErican, and the kept letters straddle the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A name can mean a person's reputation, as in making a name for yourself.

clue.text: The writer with viewpoint promoting Liberal mix

parts.note: the writer refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: promoting lifts the Liberal's letter up to the front, rearranging the word

parts.note: an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: An author with a political slant boosts the Liberal mix.
explanation.walkthrough: L for Liberal moves from fourth place in ANGLE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A mélange is a French-derived word for a mixture or medley.

clue.text: Rational to accept house standard? Try several places

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the outer word holds the others

parts.note: sound as in sound judgement, sensible
HO is the abbreviation for house
par is the normal or standard level

explanation.surface: Sensibly, someone checks a home's quality by visiting several properties before choosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop around is to compare offers from several sellers before buying.

clue.text: Relative harm after undressing in the dark

parts.note: an uncle is a family member

indicators.note: undressing strips the outer layer, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: the word with its outside letters stripped

explanation.surface: A family member comes to grief after taking clothes off in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark means not understanding, so things are unclear to you.

clue.text: Straight man mostly to halt rise of self-assertiveness

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter falls away

parts.note: stop, minus its last letter

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from bottom to top, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: ego is a sense of self-importance

explanation.surface: A comedian's sidekick largely tries to curb someone's growing arrogance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a comedian's foil who feeds lines, the straight man in a double act.

clue.text: Hydrogen lost in explosion about to circulate in rod casing?

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

indicators.note: circulating sends the short word round the other way
an explosion scatters things, so these letters are blown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for the mix
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A chemistry accident loses hydrogen in a blast, which then swirls round inside a metal rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' is American slang for a handgun, so the question mark flags a gun's case.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is the leather case worn on the belt to carry a pistol.

clue.text: Clothing is hot, to some extent

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap
a bit, somewhat

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their clothes are rather warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a long robe, especially a monk's or nun's garment, so clothing.

clue.text: Up-to-date tent, with electric current, mostly cool

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a circus tent is the big top
I is the symbol for electric current in physics
cool as in unruffled; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A modern tent with mains electricity stays fairly cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means relating to current events, so up-to-date in subject matter.

clue.text: Scots not great between banks of turbid river

indicators.note: something between two others sits inside them
the banks are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
wee is the Scots word for small

explanation.surface: A small Scottish stream between muddy riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is the river forming part of the border between Scotland and England.

clue.text: Thin time acquiring Volume One's opening? Good luck as you go

indicators.note: to acquire is to take something in, so the first word wraps around the pieces

parts.note: bony as in skinny
V is the abbreviation for volume

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A long, lean period begins with the first book of a series; the clue then waves the reader off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bon voyage is the French farewell wishing a traveller a good journey.

clue.text: Control sword, switching hands

indicators.note: the two hands are left and right, so one hand's letter is traded for the other's

parts.note: steel is a poetic word for a sword
the left-hand letter L gives way to R for right

explanation.surface: A swordsman keeps command of his weapon by moving it to his other hand.
explanation.walkthrough: L for left becomes R for right at the end of STEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide a vehicle's direction, so to control it.

clue.text: Limits of truce probed by border topic

indicators.note: to be probed is to have something pushed in, so the next piece goes inside
limits are the edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
a hem is the edge or border of cloth

explanation.surface: The terms of a ceasefire are tested by the topic of a disputed frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a talk or piece of writing, so a topic.

clue.text: Fine source of confusing statements but not primarily a cheat

indicators.note: primarily points at the first letter, and not tells us to leave it off

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a riddler poses puzzling statements

explanation.surface: A man who utters baffling remarks is excellent, but not mainly a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler is a swindler, from fiddle meaning to cheat or falsify accounts.
